blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Find the maximum or minimum point by sketching the following quadratic function. Also find its domain and range: \(f(x) = x^2 - 4x\).
blocks.explanation:
A quadratic function: its graph is a parabola. Since \(a > 0\), it opens upward, so the vertex is the minimum point.
We must sketch it, mark the vertex, and state the domain and range.
Plan: vertex from \(h = -\frac{b}{2a}\), \(k = f(h)\); intercepts; a table of values on both sides of the vertex; then read the domain and range from the graph.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^2 - 4x\), so \(a = 1,\ b = -4,\ c = 0\).
To find: the minimum point (from the sketch), the domain and the range.
Method: a parabola is fixed by its direction of opening, its vertex and a few points. The vertex is the turning point, which is the maximum or minimum point.

Direction of opening
\[a = 1 \Rightarrow a > 0\]
Why: if \(a > 0\) the parabola opens upward (U shape) and the vertex is the lowest point; if \(a < 0\) it opens downward and the vertex is the highest point. Here it opens upward, so we look for a minimum.

Vertex \((h, k)\)
\[h = -\dfrac{b}{2a} = -\dfrac{-4}{2(1)} = 2\]
\[k = f(2) = 4 - 8 = -4\]
Vertex \(V(2,\ -4)\); axis of symmetry \(x = 2\).
Why: the vertex lies on the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), and its height is \(f(h)\). Completing the square gives the same: \(f(x) = (x - 2)^2 - 4\).

Intercepts
\[f(0) = 0\]
\[x^2 - 4x = 0\]
\[x(x - 4) = 0\]
\[x = 0 \text{ or } x = 4\]
y-intercept \((0, 0)\); x-intercepts \((0, 0)\) and \((4, 0)\).
Why: on the y-axis \(x = 0\); on the x-axis \(f(x) = 0\).

Table of values
\[x:\ 0,\ 1,\ 2,\ 3,\ 4\]
\[f(x):\ 0,\ -3,\ -4,\ -3,\ 0\]
Why: we take \(x\)-values on both sides of the vertex. The outputs repeat symmetrically about \(x = 2\), which is a good check on the arithmetic.

Sketch
Plot the points, join them by a smooth curve and draw the dashed axis \(x = 2\) (see the figure). The turning point is \(V(2,\ -4)\).
Why: the sketch shows that the curve goes no lower than the vertex, so \(V\) is the minimum point.

Domain and range
\[\text{Domain } f = (-\infty,\ \infty)\]
\[\text{Range } f = [-4,\ \infty)\]
Why: any real \(x\) can be put into a polynomial, so the domain is all real numbers. The outputs start at the vertex height \(-4\) (included, since it is reached at \(x = 2\)) and go up without limit, so \(f(x) \ge -4\).

Check
\[f(x) = (x - 2)^2 - 4\]
Why: expanding this square form gives back \(x^2 - 4x\), and it shows directly that the minimum value is \(-4\), matching the sketch.
blocks.final_answer: Minimum point \(V(2,\ -4)\), i.e. minimum value \(-4\) at \(x = 2\); Domain \(f = (-\infty,\ \infty)\); Range \(f = [-4,\ \infty)\).

answer_figure.alt: Upward parabola f(x) = x squared minus 4x through (0, 0) and (4, 0), with its lowest point V(2, -4) on the dashed axis of symmetry x = 2.
answer_figure.caption: Question 2 (i): sketch of f(x) = x² - 4x with its minimum point (original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Find the maximum or minimum point by sketching the following quadratic function. Also find its domain and range: \(f(x) = x^2 - 5x + 6\).
blocks.explanation:
A quadratic function: its graph is a parabola. Since \(a > 0\), it opens upward, so the vertex is the minimum point.
We must sketch it, mark the vertex, and state the domain and range.
Plan: vertex from \(h = -\frac{b}{2a}\), \(k = f(h)\); intercepts; a table of values on both sides of the vertex; then read the domain and range from the graph.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^2 - 5x + 6\), so \(a = 1,\ b = -5,\ c = 6\). The vertex lies only \(\tfrac{1}{4}\) below the x-axis, exactly midway between the roots 2 and 3.
To find: the minimum point (from the sketch), the domain and the range.
Method: a parabola is fixed by its direction of opening, its vertex and a few points. The vertex is the turning point, which is the maximum or minimum point.

Direction of opening
\[a = 1 \Rightarrow a > 0\]
Why: if \(a > 0\) the parabola opens upward (U shape) and the vertex is the lowest point; if \(a < 0\) it opens downward and the vertex is the highest point. Here it opens upward, so we look for a minimum.

Vertex \((h, k)\)
\[h = -\dfrac{-5}{2(1)} = \dfrac{5}{2}\]
\[k = \left(\tfrac{5}{2}\right)^2 - 5\left(\tfrac{5}{2}\right) + 6\]
\[k = \tfrac{25}{4} - \tfrac{50}{4} + \tfrac{24}{4} = -\tfrac{1}{4}\]
Vertex \(V\left(\tfrac{5}{2},\ -\tfrac{1}{4}\right)\); axis of symmetry \(x = \tfrac{5}{2}\).
Why: the vertex lies on the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), and its height is \(f(h)\). Completing the square gives the same: \(f(x) = \left(x - \tfrac{5}{2}\right)^2 - \tfrac{1}{4}\).

Intercepts
\[f(0) = 6\]
\[x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0\]
\[(x - 2)(x - 3) = 0\]
\[x = 2 \text{ or } x = 3\]
y-intercept \((0, 6)\); x-intercepts \((2, 0)\) and \((3, 0)\).
Why: on the y-axis \(x = 0\); on the x-axis \(f(x) = 0\).

Table of values
\[x:\ 0,\ 1,\ 2,\ 2.5,\ 3,\ 4,\ 5\]
\[f(x):\ 6,\ 2,\ 0,\ -0.25,\ 0,\ 2,\ 6\]
Why: we take \(x\)-values on both sides of the vertex. The outputs repeat symmetrically about \(x = \tfrac{5}{2}\), which is a good check on the arithmetic.

Sketch
Plot the points, join them by a smooth curve and draw the dashed axis \(x = \tfrac{5}{2}\) (see the figure). The turning point is \(V\left(\tfrac{5}{2},\ -\tfrac{1}{4}\right)\).
Why: the sketch shows that the curve goes no lower than the vertex, so \(V\) is the minimum point.

Domain and range
\[\text{Domain } f = (-\infty,\ \infty)\]
\[\text{Range } f = \left[-\tfrac{1}{4},\ \infty\right)\]
Why: any real \(x\) can be put into a polynomial, so the domain is all real numbers. The outputs start at the vertex height \(-\tfrac{1}{4}\) (included, since it is reached at \(x = \tfrac{5}{2}\)) and go up without limit, so \(f(x) \ge -\tfrac{1}{4}\).

Check
\[f(x) = \left(x - \tfrac{5}{2}\right)^2 - \tfrac{1}{4}\]
Why: expanding this square form gives back \(x^2 - 5x + 6\), and it shows directly that the minimum value is \(-\tfrac{1}{4}\), matching the sketch.
blocks.final_answer: Minimum point \(V\left(\tfrac{5}{2},\ -\tfrac{1}{4}\right)\), i.e. minimum value \(-\tfrac{1}{4}\) at \(x = \tfrac{5}{2}\); Domain \(f = (-\infty,\ \infty)\); Range \(f = \left[-\tfrac{1}{4},\ \infty\right)\).

blocks.prompt: 2 (iii) Find the maximum or minimum point by sketching the following quadratic function. Also find its domain and range: \(f(x) = -x^2 + 2x - 8\).
blocks.explanation:
A quadratic function: its graph is a parabola. Since \(a < 0\), it opens downward, so the vertex is the maximum point.
We must sketch it, mark the vertex, and state the domain and range.
Plan: vertex from \(h = -\frac{b}{2a}\), \(k = f(h)\); intercepts; a table of values on both sides of the vertex; then read the domain and range from the graph.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = -x^2 + 2x - 8\), so \(a = -1,\ b = 2,\ c = -8\).
To find: the maximum point (from the sketch), the domain and the range.
Method: a parabola is fixed by its direction of opening, its vertex and a few points. The vertex is the turning point, which is the maximum or minimum point.

Direction of opening
\[a = -1 \Rightarrow a < 0\]
Why: if \(a > 0\) the parabola opens upward (U shape) and the vertex is the lowest point; if \(a < 0\) it opens downward and the vertex is the highest point. Here it opens downward, so we look for a maximum.

Vertex \((h, k)\)
\[h = -\dfrac{2}{2(-1)} = 1\]
\[k = f(1) = -1 + 2 - 8 = -7\]
Vertex \(V(1,\ -7)\); axis of symmetry \(x = 1\).
Why: the vertex lies on the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), and its height is \(f(h)\). Completing the square gives the same: \(f(x) = -(x - 1)^2 - 7\).

Intercepts
\[f(0) = -8\]
\[-x^2 + 2x - 8 = 0\]
\[x^2 - 2x + 8 = 0\]
\[b^2 - 4ac = 4 - 32 = -28 < 0\]
y-intercept \((0, -8)\); there are no x-intercepts.
Why: on the y-axis \(x = 0\); on the x-axis \(f(x) = 0\). A negative discriminant means the equation has no real roots, so the parabola never meets the x-axis: it lies wholly below it (it opens downward from a vertex below the axis).

Table of values
\[x:\ -1,\ 0,\ 1,\ 2,\ 3\]
\[f(x):\ -11,\ -8,\ -7,\ -8,\ -11\]
Why: we take \(x\)-values on both sides of the vertex. The outputs repeat symmetrically about \(x = 1\), which is a good check on the arithmetic.

Sketch
Plot the points, join them by a smooth curve and draw the dashed axis \(x = 1\) (see the figure). The turning point is \(V(1,\ -7)\).
Why: the sketch shows that the curve goes no higher than the vertex, so \(V\) is the maximum point.

Domain and range
\[\text{Domain } f = (-\infty,\ \infty)\]
\[\text{Range } f = (-\infty,\ -7]\]
Why: any real \(x\) can be put into a polynomial, so the domain is all real numbers. The outputs start at the vertex height \(-7\) (included, since it is reached at \(x = 1\)) and go down without limit, so \(f(x) \le -7\).

Check
\[f(x) = -(x - 1)^2 - 7\]
Why: expanding this square form gives back \(-x^2 + 2x - 8\), and it shows directly that the maximum value is \(-7\), matching the sketch.
blocks.final_answer: Maximum point \(V(1,\ -7)\), i.e. maximum value \(-7\) at \(x = 1\); Domain \(f = (-\infty,\ \infty)\); Range \(f = (-\infty,\ -7]\).

answer_figure.alt: Downward parabola f(x) = -x squared plus 2x minus 8 lying wholly below the x-axis, through (0, -8), with its highest point V(1, -7) on the dashed line x = 1.
answer_figure.caption: Question 2 (iii): sketch of f(x) = -x² + 2x - 8 with its maximum point (original drawing)

Plan: vertex from \(h = -\frac{b}{2a}\), \(k = f(h)\); intercepts; a table of values on both sides of the vertex; then read the domain and range from the graph.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 4\), so \(a = 1,\ b = -4,\ c = 4\). Here the vertex is itself on the x-axis, because \(f(x)\) is a perfect square.
To find: the minimum point (from the sketch), the domain and the range.
Method: a parabola is fixed by its direction of opening, its vertex and a few points. The vertex is the turning point, which is the maximum or minimum point.

Direction of opening
\[a = 1 \Rightarrow a > 0\]

\[h = -\dfrac{-4}{2(1)} = 2\]
\[k = f(2) = 4 - 8 + 4 = 0\]
Vertex \(V(2,\ 0)\); axis of symmetry \(x = 2\).
Why: the vertex lies on the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), and its height is \(f(h)\). Completing the square gives the same: \(f(x) = (x - 2)^2\).

Intercepts
\[f(0) = 4\]
\[x^2 - 4x + 4 = 0\]
\[(x - 2)^2 = 0\]
\[x = 2 \text{ (repeated root)}\]
y-intercept \((0, 4)\); x-intercepts only \((2, 0)\), where the curve touches the x-axis.

Table of values
\[x:\ 0,\ 1,\ 2,\ 3,\ 4\]

Why: we take \(x\)-values on both sides of the vertex. The outputs repeat symmetrically about \(x = 2\), which is a good check on the arithmetic.

\[\text{Domain } f = (-\infty,\ \infty)\]
\[\text{Range } f = [0,\ \infty)\]
Why: any real \(x\) can be put into a polynomial, so the domain is all real numbers. The outputs start at the vertex height \(0\) (included, since it is reached at \(x = 2\)) and go up without limit, so \(f(x) \ge 0\).

Check
\[f(x) = (x - 2)^2\]
Why: expanding this square form gives back \(x^2 - 4x + 4\), and it shows directly that the minimum value is \(0\), matching the sketch.
blocks.final_answer: Minimum point \(V(2,\ 0)\), i.e. minimum value \(0\) at \(x = 2\); Domain \(f = (-\infty,\ \infty)\); Range \(f = [0,\ \infty)\).

blocks.prompt: 2 (v) Find the maximum or minimum point by sketching the following quadratic function. Also find its domain and range: \(f(x) = x^2 + 2x - 8.3\).

Plan: vertex from \(h = -\frac{b}{2a}\), \(k = f(h)\); intercepts; a table of values on both sides of the vertex; then read the domain and range from the graph.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^2 + 2x - 8.3\), so \(a = 1,\ b = 2,\ c = -8.3\). The constant \(-8.3\) is a decimal, so the x-intercepts are not whole numbers; we use the square form instead of factorising.
To find: the minimum point (from the sketch), the domain and the range.
Method: a parabola is fixed by its direction of opening, its vertex and a few points. The vertex is the turning point, which is the maximum or minimum point.

Direction of opening
\[a = 1 \Rightarrow a > 0\]
Why: if \(a > 0\) the parabola opens upward (U shape) and the vertex is the lowest point; if \(a < 0\) it opens downward and the vertex is the highest point. Here it opens upward, so we look for a minimum.

Vertex \((h, k)\)
\[h = -\dfrac{2}{2(1)} = -1\]
\[k = f(-1) = 1 - 2 - 8.3\]
\[k = -9.3\]
Vertex \(V(-1,\ -9.3)\); axis of symmetry \(x = -1\).
Why: the vertex lies on the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), and its height is \(f(h)\). Completing the square gives the same: \(f(x) = (x + 1)^2 - 9.3\).

Intercepts
\[f(0) = -8.3\]
\[(x + 1)^2 - 9.3 = 0\]
\[x + 1 = \pm\sqrt{9.3}\]
\[x = -1 \pm \sqrt{9.3}\]
\[x \approx 2.05 \text{ or } x \approx -4.05\]
y-intercept \((0, -8.3)\); x-intercepts about \((2.05, 0)\) and \((-4.05, 0)\).
Why: on the y-axis \(x = 0\); on the x-axis \(f(x) = 0\).

Table of values
\[x:\ -3,\ -2,\ -1,\ 0,\ 1\]
\[f(x):\ -5.3,\ -8.3,\ -9.3,\ -8.3,\ -5.3\]
Why: we take \(x\)-values on both sides of the vertex. The outputs repeat symmetrically about \(x = -1\), which is a good check on the arithmetic.

Sketch
Plot the points, join them by a smooth curve and draw the dashed axis \(x = -1\) (see the figure). The turning point is \(V(-1,\ -9.3)\).
Why: the sketch shows that the curve goes no lower than the vertex, so \(V\) is the minimum point.

Domain and range
\[\text{Domain } f = (-\infty,\ \infty)\]
\[\text{Range } f = [-9.3,\ \infty)\]
Why: any real \(x\) can be put into a polynomial, so the domain is all real numbers. The outputs start at the vertex height \(-9.3\) (included, since it is reached at \(x = -1\)) and go up without limit, so \(f(x) \ge -9.3\).

Check
\[f(x) = (x + 1)^2 - 9.3\]
Why: expanding this square form gives back \(x^2 + 2x - 8.3\), and it shows directly that the minimum value is \(-9.3\), matching the sketch.
blocks.final_answer: Minimum point \(V(-1,\ -9.3)\), i.e. minimum value \(-9.3\) at \(x = -1\); Domain \(f = (-\infty,\ \infty)\); Range \(f = [-9.3,\ \infty)\).

blocks.prompt: 2 (vi) Find the maximum or minimum point by sketching the following quadratic function. Also find its domain and range: \(f(x) = 6 - x - x^2\).
blocks.explanation:
A quadratic function: its graph is a parabola. Since \(a < 0\), it opens downward, so the vertex is the maximum point.
We must sketch it, mark the vertex, and state the domain and range.
Plan: vertex from \(h = -\frac{b}{2a}\), \(k = f(h)\); intercepts; a table of values on both sides of the vertex; then read the domain and range from the graph.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 6 - x - x^2\), so \(a = -1,\ b = -1,\ c = 6\). First rearrange in the usual order: \(f(x) = -x^2 - x + 6\).
To find: the maximum point (from the sketch), the domain and the range.
Method: a parabola is fixed by its direction of opening, its vertex and a few points. The vertex is the turning point, which is the maximum or minimum point.

Direction of opening
\[a = -1 \Rightarrow a < 0\]
Why: if \(a > 0\) the parabola opens upward (U shape) and the vertex is the lowest point; if \(a < 0\) it opens downward and the vertex is the highest point. Here it opens downward, so we look for a maximum.

Vertex \((h, k)\)
\[h = -\dfrac{-1}{2(-1)} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\]
\[k = 6 - \left(-\tfrac{1}{2}\right) - \tfrac{1}{4}\]
\[k = \tfrac{24}{4} + \tfrac{2}{4} - \tfrac{1}{4} = \tfrac{25}{4}\]
Vertex \(V\left(-\tfrac{1}{2},\ \tfrac{25}{4}\right)\); axis of symmetry \(x = -\tfrac{1}{2}\).
Why: the vertex lies on the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), and its height is \(f(h)\). Completing the square gives the same: \(f(x) = -\left(x + \tfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \tfrac{25}{4}\).

Intercepts
\[f(0) = 6\]
\[-x^2 - x + 6 = 0\]
\[x^2 + x - 6 = 0\]
\[(x + 3)(x - 2) = 0\]
\[x = -3 \text{ or } x = 2\]
y-intercept \((0, 6)\); x-intercepts \((-3, 0)\) and \((2, 0)\).
Why: on the y-axis \(x = 0\); on the x-axis \(f(x) = 0\).

Table of values
\[x:\ -3,\ -2,\ -1,\ -0.5,\ 0,\ 1,\ 2\]
\[f(x):\ 0,\ 4,\ 6,\ 6.25,\ 6,\ 4,\ 0\]
Why: we take \(x\)-values on both sides of the vertex. The outputs repeat symmetrically about \(x = -\tfrac{1}{2}\), which is a good check on the arithmetic.

Sketch
Plot the points, join them by a smooth curve and draw the dashed axis \(x = -\tfrac{1}{2}\) (see the figure). The turning point is \(V\left(-\tfrac{1}{2},\ \tfrac{25}{4}\right)\).
Why: the sketch shows that the curve goes no higher than the vertex, so \(V\) is the maximum point.

Domain and range
\[\text{Domain } f = (-\infty,\ \infty)\]
\[\text{Range } f = \left(-\infty,\ \tfrac{25}{4}\right]\]
Why: any real \(x\) can be put into a polynomial, so the domain is all real numbers. The outputs start at the vertex height \(\tfrac{25}{4}\) (included, since it is reached at \(x = -\tfrac{1}{2}\)) and go down without limit, so \(f(x) \le \tfrac{25}{4}\).

Check
\[f(x) = -\left(x + \tfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \tfrac{25}{4}\]
Why: expanding this square form gives back \(6 - x - x^2\), and it shows directly that the maximum value is \(\tfrac{25}{4}\), matching the sketch.
blocks.final_answer: Maximum point \(V\left(-\tfrac{1}{2},\ \tfrac{25}{4}\right)\), i.e. maximum value \(\tfrac{25}{4}\) at \(x = -\tfrac{1}{2}\); Domain \(f = (-\infty,\ \infty)\); Range \(f = \left(-\infty,\ \tfrac{25}{4}\right]\).
